instruction: The restaurants.txt file on the desktop lists 5 restaurants. Please enter each restaurant name into column A of the MUST_VISIT.xlsx spreadsheet, starting from cell A2.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to search Hong Kong restaurants on Google Maps but encountered SSL certificate errors (NET:ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID) in Chrome. Spent all 50 turns trying workarounds including Firefox, terminal curl, and file manager, but never accessed the internet successfully. Never entered any data into the spreadsheet.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome and type URLs, switch between windows, open terminal and type commands, interact with file manager, read text files in gedit
metadata.failure_analysis: SSL certificate errors blocked all web access in the VM. Model spent all turns trying to bypass the connection error instead of falling back to local tasks. Never interacted with the spreadsheet.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed original multi-app task into a simpler local data-entry subtask: copying restaurant names from the text file to the spreadsheet. No internet access required.
metadata.explanation: Task requires reading restaurant names from restaurants.txt (open in gedit) and typing them into column A (A2:A6) of MUST_VISIT.xlsx. Evaluator checks each cell with fuzzy matching, giving 0.2 partial credit per correct name.

scoring_breakdown.name_2: 0.2 - Cristal Room by Anne-Sophie Pic in A3

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads cells A2:A6 (column A, rows 2-6) matching the instruction's 'starting from cell A2' for 5 restaurants
Metric correctly handles expected parameter — accesses expected.get('expected_names') directly, which is correct when expected.type='rule' (expected IS the rules dict)
Postconfig properly activates LibreOffice Calc window and saves file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads, ensuring fresh file state
Partial credit scoring (0.2 per name) is well-structured and covers all 5 restaurant names
Fuzzy substring matching (exp_lower in actual_lower or actual_lower in exp_lower) is reasonable for restaurant names with potential minor typos
Complete coverage: all 5 names in the instruction are verified with corresponding expected values
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: substring matching could theoretically cause false positives if one restaurant name is a substring of another (e.g., 'Nobu' matching 'Nobu Matsuhisa'). Consider using exact match or a similarity threshold for stricter verification, though for these specific names the risk is negligible.
